open_points.subject: A2 rule 3 — OffsetTimeOriginal minute field
open_points.text: minutes that are a minute of the hour
open_points.question: Which numeric minute-field values are valid, especially `00` and `60`?

witness.initial: The run timezone is UTC; `DateTimeOriginal` is `2026:11:20 12:00:00`; `OffsetTimeOriginal` is `+01:00` and matches the imported pattern.
events: The deliverer validates the offset and derives `photo_date`.
outcomes: Treat `00` as a valid minute field and deliver `11:00:00` UTC.
Treat minutes as ordinal minutes 1 through 60, reject the offset, and deliver `12:00:00` using the run timezone.
witness.observer: The calling flow and Portal see different `photo_date` values.

open_points.subject: A2 rule 3 — representable camera date and time
open_points.text: is no date and time the standard library's datetime type can hold
open_points.question: Which standard library, datetime type and version define the accepted range, and does “can hold” test only the parsed wall-clock fields or the timezone-resolved UTC instant as well?
options: The implementation language's naive datetime field range
The implementation language's timezone-aware datetime and UTC-conversion range
An explicit language-independent range stated in the design
open_points.default_guess: Use the pinned implementation runtime's datetime type and require both the parsed value and its resolved UTC instant to be representable.

open_points.subject: A2 rules 3–4 — timezone conversion outside datetime range
open_points.text: A camera value is unusable when it does not match the imported `EXIF_DATETIME_PATTERN` constant whole or is no date and time the standard library's datetime type can hold, so a leap second is unusable, when its UTC year is before the imported `CAMERA_EARLIEST_YEAR` constant, or when it is more than the imported `CAMERA_LATEST_AFTER_MODIFIED_HOURS` constant of hours after the file's modification time.
open_points.question: What happens when the parsed local camera date is representable but applying its EXIF or run-timezone offset produces a UTC instant outside the datetime type's representable range?
options: Treat that camera value as unusable and try the next source
Fail the delivery with a specified PlacementFailure
Define conversion over an extended instant range before applying the year checks
open_points.default_guess: Treat the camera value as unusable and try the next photo-moment source.

witness.initial: A decodable source has a representable boundary-year `DateTimeOriginal` and a valid offset whose application would move the UTC result outside the datetime type's range; a usable file modification time is present.
events: The deliverer parses the local camera value and applies the offset.
outcomes: The conversion boundary makes the camera value unusable, so the modification time becomes `photo_date`.
The parsed camera value passed the stated holdability check, and UTC conversion raises an unclassified delivery error.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees either a successful placement with a fallback date or an error.

open_points.subject: A2 rules 3–4 and A7 rule 4 — modification-time representability
open_points.text: The photo moment is the first usable value of: EXIF `DateTimeOriginal`, EXIF `DateTime`, then the file's modification time.
open_points.question: What must the delivery do when the file modification instant cannot be represented by the required datetime form, either while comparing a camera value with it or when using it as the fallback photo moment?
options: Fail the photo with a named PlacementFailure
Refuse the whole operation with a named RefusalCode
Define a representable modification-time range and make values outside it unusable or invalid
open_points.default_guess: Define the supported modification-time range and return a specific per-photo failure when it is outside that range.

witness.initial: A decodable source has no usable camera date and has a filesystem modification instant outside the datetime type's representable range.
events: The deliverer reaches the modification-time fallback and must create `taken_at`.
outcomes: The deliverer reports a per-photo failure chosen by the implementer.
The conversion exception becomes a whole-operation or server error chosen by another implementer.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees different outcome types and codes.

open_points.subject: A2 INV-04 Required tests
open_points.text: INV-04: camera times with an offset, without one, implausible or absent give the expected UTC value (`test_the_photo_date_is_naive_utc`).
open_points.question: Which exact inputs, timezone, boundary cases and UTC results must this test assert, including offset-minute boundaries, leap seconds, datetime-range boundaries, UTC-conversion overflow and modification-time fallback?
options: Specify a closed fixture table with the expected UTC result for every named case
Specify only representative ordinary cases and add separate tests for every changed boundary
Leave the cases and expected values to the test implementer
open_points.default_guess: Provide a closed fixture table covering ordinary values and every acceptance or fallback boundary introduced by rule 3.
